PullRequest.Title: chat: stabilize reference details loading and share pill hovers
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Reference collections should remain useful while details load, without repeated loading placeholders or replacing the controls a user is interacting with. This change keeps reference IDs visible from the start and shares the row and hover behavior across collections and both chat surfaces.

- Show stable leading IDs with recorded or neutral labels, then enrich supported references with provider metadata.
- Warm newly recorded GitHub references with bounded, core-only background requests. Promote interactive requests through both the resolver and transport queues, retain stale details during refresh, and invalidate retained data when references or the default client change.
- Share pill presentation, hover ownership, actions, and popup padding for GitHub references, commits, files, images, URLs, settings, and customizations. Keep GitHub URL recognition and fetching inside the resource-details adapter.
- Update declared status and CI regions in place while preserving open-card titles, keyboard controls, and focus. Announce changed status politely without replacing unchanged live-region content. Preserve content-based sizing for collection lists and ordinary text previews; rich GitHub cards retain their existing responsive width.

No new settings, commands, reference-provider registry, or public extension API are introduced. Non-GitHub recorded labels and GitHub commit-message enrichment retain their existing behavior.

Related: #339342, #337983.

## Testing

1. In Component Explorer, open `sessions/chatReferences` and compare **Cold Reference Titles** with **Resolved Reference Titles**. Verify leading IDs, meaningful fallback labels, title truncation, status icons, and copy/remove actions.
2. In Code OSS, select the local Copilot harness and the VS Code workspace. Record several GitHub PR and issue references, then open **References** immediately. Hover or focus a later row while earlier requests are pending; its detail request should receive interactive priority.
3. Reopen a warm card, then repeat after the freshness window: 30 seconds for PR details and 60 seconds for issues. Cached content should remain available during refresh. Live status updates must not replace the title or focused controls.
4. Check dedicated PR/issue collections and a mixed References collection containing a commit, file, image, URL, settings URI, and non-GitHub link in both Agents and editor windows. For customization paths, turn on **Customizations** in the pill visibility menu.
5. Use arrow keys, Tab/Shift+Tab, and Escape to navigate and dismiss previews. Check a reference without available GitHub metadata: its identity and open/copy/remove actions should remain usable. Removing a record must not delete its underlying resource.

## Visual evidence

The attached interactive-fixture clip shows the References popup staying mounted as PR details resolve and selection moves to an issue preview. It uses controlled mock GitHub latency, not live GitHub or native OSS evidence.

Live GitHub/account-switch, native screen-reader, and full integration/smoke flows were not run locally. See the [component-fixture screenshot comparison](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/340433#issuecomment-6052575157).

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6cb3e8c-3845-4ced-a023-63e27aa6e8a7

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added cache call, session-scoped retain set, and `_views` ownership are directly traced. ActionList treats HTMLElement hover content as caller-owned and removes it without disposing it on ordinary navigation, while `CachedChatPillHover` has no cleanup for detached views. The exact retained bytes depend on how many commit previews a user visits, so severity is low rather than speculative omission.
Findings.PerformanceResource: detached rich-hover DOM nodes, tabbable element arrays, onclick handlers, and callback closures
Findings.PerformanceScaling: O(H) retained rich DOM trees where H is the number of distinct commit entries hovered while they remain in the session; each commit can retain compact and default views.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: retained memory and increasing GC pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Commit previews were created for the active hover and were not inserted into a session-scoped per-commit hover cache, so closing the preview did not leave its rich DOM reachable from a cache for the remainder of the session.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Commit rows in the agent-host References/Artifacts collections now use a session-scoped `ChatPillHoverCache`, so rendering a commit preview permanently populates a cached view for that commit until the commit disappears or the session changes.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added commit path wraps every commit entry with `this._commitHoverCache.get(...)` at line 1080. `ChatPillHoverCache` retains each key for the whole current session, and each cached entry's `_views` map keeps the rendered compact/default HTMLElement trees after they are detached; unlike the previous commit hover closure, no close/dispose hook clears those views.
Findings.Title: Release cached commit cards when their hover closes
Findings.Impact: In a long agent session with many commit references, navigating through commit previews leaves every visited card retained after it closes. Memory and later GC work grow with preview history, increasing the workbench's footprint for the rest of the session.
Findings.Evidence: `AgentHostSessionInputPills` retains `_commitHoverCache` keys for all current commit artifacts/references and line 1080 inserts the cache presentation into each commit. `CachedChatPillHover._render` stores the rich element and its tabbable/live children in `_views`; subsequent closure of the submenu only detaches caller-owned HTMLElement content, and neither `hover` nor `pillHover` supplies a lifecycle callback that deletes the view. Rich commit cards contain multiple DOM nodes, onclick handlers, and callbacks capturing the session services.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the stable descriptor/action cache, but evict each density's view when its hover closes or becomes detached; retain a view only while connected so reopening reconstructs fresh content without preserving closed-card DOM.

Scenarios.Scenario: Record or receive new GitHub references in Agents/editor session surfaces
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Background warming is off the immediate record/update path. A cold hover awaits resolution for rich content; a warm hover renders retained content synchronously and refreshes stale or incomplete data in place.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire the default GitHub client/credential and refresh issue or pull-request fragments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One issue REST refresh or one PR core GraphQL refresh per newly added unique GitHub reference; PR hover completion may then perform core plus checks refreshes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Reference details were resolved lazily on hover/dropdown prefetch rather than automatically warmed when newly recorded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Warm requests are background. Cold hover resolution is on the rich-preview path; cached content remains immediately usable during refresh.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of unique newly recorded canonical GitHub issue/PR references after a session is loaded.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A resolver-wide Limiter admits at most 3 background prefetches. Interactive intent can promote queued work, while the transport still caps global requests at 4, host concurrency at 2, and caller concurrency at 2 with reserved interactive capacity.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The resolver keeps positive issue/PR details per normalized target while retained. Background results are reusable for 15 minutes; interactive freshness is 60 seconds for issues and 30 seconds for PRs. Initial/restored history and loading history are not warmed, duplicate targets coalesce in the resolver, eviction aborts queued/running work, and account changes clear state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: retain gating, per-target cache keys, limiter behavior, promotion, fragment refreshes, and transport limits are explicit and covered by tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sessions normally contain few references, but providers can append a batch. Total calls scale with unique new references; wire concurrency is bounded, so no concurrency-burst finding was warranted.
Scenarios.Verdict: The PR intentionally adds bounded off-path warming. It increases total network work but guards restored history, deduplicates targets, cancels evicted work, and limits concurrency; no independent actionable regression was reported.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and navigate References, Pull Requests, or Issues dropdowns
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Constructing the list is synchronous UI work. Cold rich hover requests are critical to full card content; warm cards render immediately. Label/status updates rebuild list items without geometry reads or forced layout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke entry-specific GitHub prefetch callbacks before/on row visibility.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to five prefetch callbacks per dropdown opening, deduplicated by entry id for that opening and by resolver target/freshness across openings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The dropdown already prefetched eligible entries; the PR changes resolver sharing, warming, and promotion behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Prefetch is off the initial list-opening critical path; focused/hovered cold entries wait for the matching promoted request.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Collection row count and number of cold eligible GitHub entries, capped to five dropdown-initiated prefetches.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most five entries are requested by dropdown prefetch, with resolver background concurrency 3 and transport host concurrency 2. Interactive requests are promoted rather than restarted.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Opening a collection prefetches at most the first five eligible entries, while resolver freshness prevents duplicate issue work and promotes matching queued work. PR core-only warm data is retained and displayed while checks/core are refreshed for interactive completeness.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for request/cardinality behavior; moderate for collection sizes, which is why no UI-CPU finding was submitted.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large reference collections cause repeated list reconstruction as metadata resolves, but no changed forced-layout or sufficiently costly synchronous mechanism was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Promotion, deduplication, and bounded prefetch avoid a reportable boundary fan-out or synchronous-rendering regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browse rich commit previews across a long agent session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Creating a rich commit card occurs when its hover is rendered. Reopening uses retained DOM, but ordinary hover close only detaches caller-owned content and does not release the cache view.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct commit entries previewed while their records remain in a long-lived session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No asynchronous concurrency is involved in commit card construction; one compact/default view can be retained per visited commit key.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ChatPillHoverCache keeps descriptors/actions and rendered density views by entry key until retain removes the key or scope changes. PR/issue caching largely replaces prior behavior; commit caching is newly applied in both session surfaces.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the commit cache calls, session-scoped retain sets, `_views` map, and ActionList caller-owned HTMLElement lifecycle were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The bytes per card and typical number of visited commits vary, but retention and O(visited commits) scaling are certain; this uncertainty was reflected in low severity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable cache-lifecycle regression: detached rich cards and their handlers remain reachable for each visited commit until session/key eviction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Preview image, file, URL, and customization references
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The image filesystem read and decode start only when preview content is requested, so they are on the selected image-preview path but not list rendering/startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read up to 20 MiB from the preview resource and decode image hover content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One capped file read per opened image preview, reused while that preview descriptor remains cached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Image previews already performed the same lazy capped read; the PR moves shared presentation helpers without increasing read cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The selected image preview waits for the local read/decode; collection rendering does not.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of image previews actively opened, normally one dropdown hover at a time.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One read per active cached image preview; switching/eviction disposes the prior preview. No new multi-image burst was introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Image hover content is cached per current entry/hover descriptor and disposed on resource-hover eviction; reads are canceled through the hover token/disposable. Location/customization hovers contain only bounded text DOM.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High after tracing helper callers and disposal paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: File size varies up to the existing 20 MiB cap, but the changed code does not increase reads or move them earlier.
Scenarios.Verdict: No diff-caused filesystem, allocation, or eager-work regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 35 changed files. Traced GitHub warm/interactive request scheduling, transport boundaries and limits, dropdown/render paths, image filesystem reads, and hover cache ownership. Submitted one low-severity commit-hover cache-lifecycle finding; bounded network warming and promotion did not meet the regression threshold.
